dispatched_notes: Sources disagree. AAM mission page (388-03): 388BG (18). Memoir of S/Sgt Eugene T. Carson, 560th BS (388-02): "We were scheduled to put up twenty-two aircraft and be the low group" of the lead combat wing (96th BG furnishing lead and high groups); one take-off crash (42-30193) and five mechanical aborts left 16 aircraft, all of which reached the target; 3 landed at other airfields; no 388th aircraft lost in the air. Lost = 0 in combat (PROBABLE; no 388th entry in the b17flyingfortress.de loss list 388-05 other than 42-30709, which had been transferred to the 96th BG on 21/8/43); 1 written off on take-off.
formation_notes: Low group of the lead 3rd BD combat wing, with the 96th BG as lead and high groups (388-02, single source).

aircraft.loss_details: Crashed on take-off for Schweinfurt at Knettishall; No. 3 engine caught fire (388-02); crew escaped uninjured, 11 returned to duty; aircraft salvaged (388-01). The take-off crash delayed the rest of the group while the area was cleared (388-02). AAM mission page (388-03) records one 3rd BD aircraft crashed on take-off, DBR, 11 RTD.
aircraft.notes: Assigned 561BS/388BG 15/6/43 (AAM 388-01). Aircraft letter "R" from AAM "Markings & paint scheme: R"; squadron code letters not given there. Nickname "Hard Luck" in AAM and in the 388th memoir (388-02) for this incident. The aircraft's regular crew (Eccleston) is NOT this mission's crew; only Molinari of that crew is in the take-off-crash list. Most of the Swift crew are shown on AAM person pages as 566th BS (as given; not resolved).

aircraft.notes: Single memoir source for this sortie (Eugene T. Carson, tail gunner, 388-02): flew "Tiger Girl", serial given as 42-3555, described as a new B-17G with chin turret. AAM (388-04) gives 42-3555 Tiger Girl as B-17F-75-DL, 560BS/388BG, assigned 9/43, MIA Bremen 26/11/43 (MACR 3116) - type recorded as B-17F per AAM (late Douglas F-models had chin turrets). Memoir states all 16 attacking 388th aircraft reached the target; three landed away from base; Carson's guns were nearly out of ammunition. Damage to this aircraft not described.

research_gaps: Only 2 of the 388th's ~18-22 aircraft identified. The 388th BG database (www.388bg.com, linked from the 388th BG Association site 388thbga.org) has mission, formation (pageType=formation) and crew pages, but every data page requires registration/login with an email address; I did not register (account creation not permitted for me). The user could register and look up the 14 Oct 1943 mission (likely mission id pattern 388-M0xx) and its formation page - that would probably give the full load list and formation.
388thbg.org / 388bg.org (named in the brief) do not resolve; www.388thbg.org has an expired TLS certificate; www.388bg.info is a parked/redirecting domain (not followed).
AAM aircraft pages linked to the mission returned only 388th airframes with no 14 Oct 1943 activity except 42-30193; AAM mission connection lists are sparse.
Tiger Girl crew beyond pilot, co-pilot, engineer and tail gunner not confirmed for this date (rest taken from a 9 Sep 1943 roster, marked UNVERIFIED).
Which 5 aircraft aborted and which 3 landed away are not identified.
Ranks and service numbers largely unknown.
Carson memoir (388-02) parts beyond the Schweinfurt chapter not read in full; it is the only per-mission narrative found.
